title: Frobenius/Zolotarev for squarefree odd n: sign(x ↦ a·x on ℤ/n) = J(a | n)
description: Performs the factorization induction that the parent (the prime base case sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a) explicitly left as a follow-up, landing on Mathlib's actual jacobiSym. For every ODD SQUAREFREE modulus n and integer a coprime to n, the sign of the multiplication-by-a permutation of the whole ring ℤ/n equals the Jacobi symbol J(a | n) — the genuine Frobenius (1914) generalization of Zolotarev's lemma. The proof is strong induction on n via its smallest prime factor p = n.minFac, recursing on the cofactor m = n/p (coprime to p because n is squarefree): the grandparent's CRT multiplicativity sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd splits the sign across n = p·m, the parent's base case anchors the prime factor to a Legendre symbol, the inductive hypothesis handles the cofactor, and jacobiSym.mul_right reassembles the product into J(a | n). The recursion bottoms out at n = 1 (ℤ/1 is a subsingleton, sign = 1 = J(a | 1)).

overview.text: The general odd-squarefree statement is exactly the recursive structure of the Jacobi symbol itself. Mathlib defines jacobiSym a n as the product of legendreSym over the prime factors of n; the permutation side mirrors this exactly: sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd (denominator multiplicativity at the level of permutation signs) is the structural shadow of jacobiSym.mul_right (denominator multiplicativity of the symbol), and the recursion bottoms out at the single prime base case proved by the parent. The whole content is the bookkeeping that an odd squarefree number splits off its smallest prime factor coprimely.
overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev (1872) identified the Legendre symbol (a/p) with the sign of x ↦ ax on (ℤ/p)ˣ. Frobenius (1914) generalized this to composite moduli and the Jacobi symbol, using the Chinese Remainder Theorem. The lineage of gallery entries built this up in layers: the grandparent (oq-01-oq-03) formalized the structural CRT decomposition of the multiplication permutation on the whole ring ℤ/n; the parent (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01) proved the prime base case sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a and closed the loop for a two-prime modulus, explicitly leaving the general squarefree case as 'a routine induction over the prime factorization adding no new idea.' This entry performs that induction and reaches Mathlib's jacobiSym.
overview.problemStatement: Open Question (the listed next step of elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01-oq-03-oq-01): iterate sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd over the full prime factorization to obtain sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for all squarefree odd n.
overview.proofStrategy: Strong induction on n (Nat.strong_induction_on). Base n = 1: ℤ/1 is a subsingleton, so ringMulPerm u is the identity, its sign is 1, and jacobiSym.one_right gives J(a | 1) = 1. Step n > 1: take the smallest prime factor p = n.minFac and the cofactor m = n/p. Squarefreeness forces Coprime p m (if p ∣ m then p² ∣ n, contradicting Squarefree), and n = p·m odd gives both factors odd with m < n. Manufacture the CRT component units u₁ : (ℤ/p)ˣ, u₂ : (ℤ/m)ˣ from coprimality (intCast_isUnit_of_isCoprime, a small Bezout bridge), matching the Chinese-remainder projections via map_intCast. Then sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd splits sign(ringMulPerm u) = sign(ringMulPerm u₁) · sign(ringMulPerm u₂); the parent's base case rewrites the p-factor as legendreSym p a = J(a | p), the inductive hypothesis rewrites the m-factor as J(a | m), and jacobiSym.mul_right reassembles J(a | p) · J(a | m) = J(a | p·m) = J(a | n).
keyInsights: The general squarefree statement is the recursion of the Jacobi symbol made structural: jacobiSym.mul_right (the symbol's denominator multiplicativity) is the value-level shadow of sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd (the CRT multiplicativity of the permutation sign), and both bottom out at the prime base case.

Squarefreeness is exactly what makes the smallest prime factor split off coprimely: p ∣ (n/p) would give p² ∣ n, so Squarefree n forces Coprime p (n/p) — the hypothesis the CRT lemma needs at every step.
Manufacturing the per-prime component units costs only a one-line Bezout bridge: an integer coprime to k casts to a unit of ℤ/k, because x·a + y·k = 1 reduces mod k to x·a = 1.

Using the integer representative a throughout makes the Chinese-remainder component-matching automatic: the first projection of (a : ℤ/n) is (a : ℤ/p), by map_intCast, so no residue bookkeeping is needed.
Landing on Mathlib's jacobiSym (rather than a hand-rolled product) ties the permutation-sign computation directly to the library's Jacobi-symbol API.
prerequisites: The parent's prime base case (ZolotarevBaseCase.sign_ringMulPerm_eq_legendre) and legendreSym_unit_eq
The grandparent's CRT multiplicativity (ZolotarevCRT.sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd) and legendre_eq_jacobi
The Jacobi symbol and its denominator multiplicativity (jacobiSym.mul_right, jacobiSym.one_right)
Smallest-prime-factor arithmetic (Nat.minFac_prime, Nat.minFac_dvd) and squarefree divisor facts

sections.title: The integer unit from a coprimality hypothesis
sections.content: intCast_isUnit_of_isCoprime: if an integer c is coprime to k, then (c : ℤ/k) is a unit. Bezout's x·c + y·k = 1 reduces mod k (where k = 0) to x·c = 1, exhibiting the inverse. This manufactures the CRT component units at each prime factor.

sections.title: The main induction
sections.content: main: strong induction on n via its smallest prime factor. The n = 1 base uses the subsingleton structure of ℤ/1; the inductive step splits n = p·m coprimely, applies the grandparent's CRT multiplicativity, the parent's prime base case, the inductive hypothesis on the cofactor, and jacobiSym.mul_right to assemble J(a | n).

sections.title: Clean statement
sections.content: sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym: the result in ordinary binder form — for n odd squarefree, c coprime to n, and the unit u representing c, sign(ringMulPerm u) = J(c | n).

meta.author: Zolotarev (1872), Frobenius (1914)
meta.assumptions: None. The file has 0 axiom declarations, 0 sorries, no native_decide, and no assumption-carrying structures. All results are fully machine-checked against Mathlib v4.26.0 (#print axioms on main and sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym reports only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound). Honest scope: the squarefree case is complete and unconditional. Prime-power factors p^e (e ≥ 2) of a fully general odd n are NOT handled — the Chinese Remainder Theorem only separates coprime factors, and the sign of multiplication on ℤ/p^e is a genuinely different computation (not bookkeeping), left to a follow-up. No new axioms are introduced.

conclusion.summary: Proves, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the full Frobenius/Jacobi generalization of Zolotarev's lemma for squarefree odd moduli: sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for every odd squarefree n, landing on Mathlib's jacobiSym. The proof is strong induction on n via its smallest prime factor, combining the parent's prime base case with the grandparent's CRT multiplicativity and jacobiSym.mul_right.
conclusion.implications: Completes the squarefree-odd case of the Frobenius/Zolotarev generalization that the lineage built up in layers: the CRT decomposition (grandparent) supplies the multiplicative structure, the prime base case (parent) anchors each factor to a Legendre value, and this entry's factorization induction reassembles them into the genuine Jacobi symbol. The result identifies the whole-ring multiplication-permutation sign with Mathlib's jacobiSym for all odd squarefree n.
openQuestions: Handle prime-power factors p^e (e ≥ 2): the CRT does not split them, and the sign of multiplication on ℤ/p^e (where (ℤ/p^e)ˣ has even order) is a genuinely new computation — reaching this would give sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for every odd n.
Specialize the squarefree statement to recover quadratic reciprocity itself (Zolotarev's original application) via the supplementary laws and the sign of the negation/shift permutations.
Repair the bit-rotted grandparent file ElementaryQuadraticReciprocityOQ01 so the units-level lemma in the lineage need not be duplicated.
